gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, by Club Car's own Onward spec pages, a lead-acid Onward keeps only about 25–38% of its first-year range after four years while the lithium versions keep 80–92%, or that the $1,150–$1,580 48V conversion kits store 5.12–5.38 kWh, 28–34% more than the Onward's 4.0 kWh base lithium pack, at $225–$294 per kWh.
standout_why: I compared against the cited clubcar.com/en-us/personal/golf-carts page (prices and speeds only, no kWh, range or weight), clubcar.com/en/lithium-ion (only speed, the 375 A controller and IP67, no capacity), ttgolfcarts.com inventory (no lithium listings with specs) and the Advantage Golf Cars E-Z-GO Liberty ELiTE listing (price and 8-year battery warranty, no capacity). None gives pack kWh, charger watts, the lead-acid vs lithium weight gap, the range after four years, or cost per kWh. ChatGPT's own answer gave generic ranges ('30–60 miles', '3–6 hours') with no model-specific numbers.
decides: This backs ChatGPT's 'lithium over lead-acid' advice with Club Car's own figures: on the Onward, lithium sheds 248–310 lb and holds most of its range after four years, while lead-acid ends up with about a third. For the 'upgrade an existing cart' branch, which ChatGPT offered but never priced, the Redodo 48V 100Ah kit ($1,149.99, $225/kWh, 5.6 h refill) beats the Vatrer 48V 105Ah kit ($1,579.99, $294/kWh, about 5.8 h) on cost per kWh. Either kit holds more energy than Club Car's 4.0 kWh base lithium, though less than its 7.0 kWh XR pack.
